preflight.name: kit tests
preflight.why: the rules in CLAUDE.md are only pinned by these tests; a release ships the rules

preflight.name: beta review slot
preflight.why: only one build per version can sit in Beta App Review (ANOTHER_BUILD_IN_REVIEW) — the next build joins the external group once the previous review finishes

notes: No suit symbols in any App Store Connect text — description, promotional text and TestFlight What to Test all reject the four suit characters (409 invalid characters), and a '<' in the description is refused as markup. Write '3 of diamonds'.

No 'Palm' anywhere a user or reviewer can read (guideline 2.3.10): app strings, store metadata, TestFlight What to Test. Say 'the 1999 handheld game'. Type names, comments and the GitHub repo are fine — which is why TestFlight notes carry the commit hash, not the branch name.
Export with the *other* key in ~/.appstoreconnect/private_keys/, not $ASC_KEY_ID: that one is App Manager and the export fails with 'Cloud signing permission error'. Same issuer id for both.
Every territory except mainland China (a game there needs a license number).

Xcode Cloud archives every push to main (GitHub check run "BigTwo | Default | Archive - iOS"). Metadata and screenshots are still web-only — there is no fastlane here, and the release notes are kept in docs/release_notes/<version>-<locale>.txt to be pasted in.

An iPhone SE / 6s on iOS 15 showed no screenshots at all: the old App Store client does not fall back to the 6.9" set, so the listing needs its own 4.7" (750x1334) images — they cover 4.7" and, through Apple's fallback chain, 4". No runtime here can capture them any more (iOS 27 refuses every 4.7" simulator), so `python3 scripts/make_47_screenshots.py` re-cuts the 6.9" shots: it drops bands of the flat bezel until the frame is 16:9, then scales. Files are `iphone47_*` — fastlane deliver files them by pixel size, asc.swift by that prefix.

Store text and per-locale screenshots live in docs/store/ (see its README). Metadata is typed into App Store Connect by hand; the screenshots can go through asc.swift once an API key exists on the machine. Each locale must be created in App Store Connect before either can be uploaded, Filipino is not an App Store metadata language at all (no fil/tl in fastlane's ALL_LANGUAGES), so docs/store/fil is reference only.

Two API keys live in ~/.appstoreconnect/private_keys/, issuer 69a6de76-aec0-47e3-e053-5b8c7c11a4d1. ASC_KEY_ID=3URS293Q46 calls the API and cannot cloud-sign (export exit 70). Export and altool use UB93M4QPXW. altool only searches that private_keys folder.

deliver refuses the whole screenshots directory because of the fil/ folder: 'Unsupported directory name(s) for screenshots/metadata: fil'. Copy the six store locales to a staging directory outside the repo and pass --screenshots_path, or the upload never starts. docs/store/README.md says not to upload fil; it does not say fil's mere presence breaks deliver.

fastlane pilot builds still crashes on 2.240.1, not only 2.236.x — 'betaBuildMetrics is not a valid relationship name' (fastlane #21104). Without an API key the build list has to come from a small spaceship script.

Spaceship::ConnectAPI::Build.all ignores the sort: parameter and can return a stale page — a query for the newest builds answered with 1.1 builds from nine days earlier while six 1.2 builds already existed. Filter on the version explicitly and do not conclude a build is missing from one listing.

⚠️ A Ruby error raised inside spaceship prints the whole client object, Apple ID password in plaintext included. Never write a script that lets an exception dump a spaceship client — rescue and print e.message only.

Xcode Cloud numbers builds itself and there is no clean build-to-commit link. Match each build's uploadedDate against the GitHub 'Archive - iOS' check run's completed_at: the upload lands about two minutes before the run completes.
